newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's spread may widen, then seen falling - poll.
newsitem.headline: Spain's spread may widen, then seen falling - poll.

text.p: The 10-year cash spread between Spanish bonds and their German counterpart could widen toward 150 basis points in one week, but later may move back to around 120 basis points in one month's time.
A poll of 10 analysts conducted on Monday found that recent turmoil in Spain's debt and peseta market is thought likely to be short-lived.
Analysts also thought the possibility of a delay in European monetary union was penalising Spain more than other countries.
"Spain is not expected to delay its entry, but if they put off the whole project, Spain will be punished," said Luca Jellinek, economist at Paribas Capital Markets in London.

At around 1200 GMT the 10-year spread was trading at around 139 basis points, in a technical correction from 145 bps on Friday evening. The peseta was trading at around 84.85/88 per mark after the mark touched a high at 84.92.
At that level the Bank of Spain was reported to have bought pesetas to stop it from weakening.
The peseta could try to break 85.10 per mark short-term, but dealers agreed the Bank of Spain will defend the 85 level.
A key money rate cut in the short term is likely to be delayed, according to six out of ten analysts.
The other four still think that after the February CPI data, due on March 13, the Bank of Spain could cut again.
But others said it would delay any move until the markets calm down a little.
